zoom.label: Napoleon's crimson mantle, below his waist

c1.text: Level one: Napoleon at the centre, in his great crimson velvet mantle. Zoom in on the small gold shapes scattered over it.

zoom.label: Napoleon's crimson mantle, below his waist

c1q.text: What are the little gold shapes on the mantle?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record INV 3699, 'Le Couronnement de l'empereur Napoléon Ier et de l'impératrice Joséphine...' (commentary by Côme Fabre, 2025; description quoting the 1808 Salon booklet; our translations)
Mémoires de madame de Rémusat 1802-1808, ed. Paul de Rémusat (Paris: Calmann Lévy, 1880), vol. II (lady-in-waiting to Josephine, an eyewitness; our translations)
Jérémie Benoît, 'Le Sacre de Napoléon', Histoire par l'image (histoire-image.org), September 2020 (our translations)

c1m.text: Gold bees on crimson velvet: on his mantle, and on Josephine's cushion too.

c1a.text: Eagles were an Empire emblem, but not these.

correction.tempting: The Empire had its eagles: David's other coronation picture is the Distribution of the Eagles.
correction.truth: The mantle is crimson velvet strewn with gold bees, as the official 1808 booklet described it.
correction.evidence: 1808 booklet, quoted in the Louvre record: a mantle 'strewn with gold bees'. Madame de Rémusat, an eyewitness: a purple mantle 'sown with bees'.

c1b.text: Yes: gold bees on crimson velvet, as the 1808 booklet lists them. The cushion Josephine kneels on is sown with bees too.

c1c.text: Laurel is on his head, not scattered here.

correction.tempting: He wears a wreath of gold laurels, so laurel embroidery would match.
correction.truth: The shapes on the mantle are bees: crimson velvet 'strewn with gold bees', in the 1808 booklet's words.
correction.evidence: 1808 booklet, quoted in the Louvre record. Madame de Rémusat, who was there: a purple mantle 'sown with bees'.

zoom.label: Napoleon's head and the crown he holds up

c2.text: Level one: Napoleon has already crowned himself. Zoom in on his head, just beside the crown he holds up.

zoom.label: Napoleon's head and the crown he holds up

c2q.text: What is Napoleon wearing on his own head?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record INV 3699, 'Le Couronnement de l'empereur Napoléon Ier et de l'impératrice Joséphine...' (commentary by Côme Fabre, 2025; description quoting the 1808 Salon booklet; our translations)
Mémoires de madame de Rémusat 1802-1808, ed. Paul de Rémusat (Paris: Calmann Lévy, 1880), vol. II (lady-in-waiting to Josephine, an eyewitness; our translations)
E.-J. Delécluze, Louis David, son école et son temps. Souvenirs (Paris: Didier, 1855), ch. X (our translations)

c2m.text: Golden laurels on his head; the crown in his hands goes to Josephine.

correction.tempting: He's still holding a crown up, as if the crowning were yet to come.
correction.truth: He has already crowned himself: on his head is his crown of golden laurels; the raised crown is for Josephine.
correction.evidence: Louvre record: he put on his crown of golden laurels, then took the empress's crown. Delécluze (1855): Napoleon 'already crowned'.

c2b.text: Yes: a crown of golden laurels. Madame de Rémusat, who was there, said it was formed like the Caesars' crown of laurel.

c2c.text: The crown in his hands is for someone else.

correction.tempting: A new emperor would surely wear the grandest crown he had.
correction.truth: On his head is a wreath of golden laurels; the crown he holds up is about to crown Josephine.
correction.evidence: Louvre record: the golden laurels on his head, the empress's crown in his hands. Madame de Rémusat: a simple laurel crown encircled his head.

extends.concept: The emblems on the coronation robes

c1q.what_you_learn: Napoleon's crimson velvet mantle is strewn with gold bees (and so is Josephine's cushion); eagles and laurels are other emblems of the day, elsewhere.
